q: How do we adjust air conditioning energy for a hotter year?
title: Weather-normalising cooling energy
short: Use cooling degree days. They add up how far each day's temperature was above a base, often 18 to 24 C. Plot monthly cooling kWh against degree days for a past year. The fitted line shows what a normal year would use, so a hot summer does not hide a real saving.
audience: Offices, hotels, hospitals and cold stores

ul: Separate cooling kWh by sub-meter, or estimate it from summer and winter bills.
Get monthly degree days for the nearest weather station.
Fit kWh against degree days and report actual and normalised figures.

p: Report actual emissions in the inventory. Use the normalised figure only to explain performance, and label it.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and electricity bills and applies IPCC 2006 factors and the CEA grid factor (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25), so you can compare Scope 1 and 2 before and after a change from the documents themselves.
